issues.title: Run JoinDependentFilterRule before DistributivityRule
issues.hypothesis: In q19 the whole OR-of-ANDs predicate is evaluated in a FILTER above the lineitem⋈part HASH_JOIN (0.42s). The join emits 2.14M rows (0.68s), but only 1,170 survive. JoinDependentFilterRule derives per-table OR filters (for example (p_brand='Brand#45' AND ...) OR (...) on part, and the l_quantity range OR on lineitem). It only fires on a root OR, though. DistributivityRule is registered earlier (optimizer.cpp:52 vs :69) and factors the common p_partkey=l_partkey term out first, so the root becomes an AND and nothing is derived. A previous evolve run measured the reordered version: q19 336->157ms (-53%), join output 2.14M->2.7K rows.
issues.plan: In src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp, move `rewriter.rules.push_back(make_uniq<JoinDependentFilterRule>(rewriter));` (line 69) to just before the DistributivityRule push_back (line 52). Nothing else changes. Check that the q19 plan now shows derived filters on the part scan and the lineitem side, and that the result is unchanged. Run the unit tests for the optimizer and filter pushdown (test/optimizer/*, any test that mentions join_dependent).
issues.expected_gain: q19 -40..-55%, so roughly -4..-5% on the visible geomean. It may also help other disjunctive join predicates in hidden templates (TPC-H q07-style nation pairs).
issues.generality: Applies to any WHERE clause written as an OR of conjunctions that each touch several tables and repeat a join key, which is common in BI-generated SQL and in TPC-H q07/q19 patterns. The derived filters are redundant and implied, so correctness holds. The worst case is a little extra evaluation of the derived OR filters when they are not selective.
issues.risk: Low. Only the rule order changes. The expression rewriter runs the rules to a fixpoint, so Distributivity still runs afterwards. Check that no infinite rewrite loop appears (derived filters must not be re-derived) and that no plan-snapshot tests break.

issues.title: Length-aware selectivity for contains()/LIKE scan filters
issues.hypothesis: q09 (1284ms, the largest template) has p_name LIKE '%ghost%', which becomes contains(). Cardinality estimation gives this expression filter the default 0.2 selectivity, so the join order is poor. The plan shows two hash joins of about 2.6s each, on 3.27M rows. A previous run measured a length-aware estimate, sel = max(0.2*0.75^L, 0.01) in InspectTableFilter (relation_statistics_helper.cpp, EXPRESSION_FILTER case): q09 -35%.
issues.plan: In src/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.cpp, InspectTableFilter: for an ExpressionFilter whose expression is a contains/like function with a constant pattern, estimate selectivity from the literal length as above. Verify the function names in that file first.
issues.generality: Any substring filter on a dimension table feeding a join order. It could misorder joins when a short literal is very common.
issues.risk: Medium. It changes join orders in other queries that use LIKE filters.

issues.title: Perfect hash join for RIGHT joins
issues.hypothesis: q13's RIGHT HASH_JOIN (o_custkey=c_custkey; build side is customer, 1.5M dense keys) takes 1.76s, and the agg on top takes 2.21s. A perfect HJ is not used for RIGHT joins. A previous run found 3 gates (optimizer min/max propagation and an off-by-one duplicate check) and measured q13 -20%.
issues.plan: Investigate the PerfectHashJoinExecutor eligibility checks in physical_hash_join.cpp / perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp and in the join-stats propagation in the optimizer. Allow RIGHT/outer joins with dense unique build keys.
issues.generality: FK joins against dense-key dimension tables with outer semantics.
issues.risk: Medium. Needs correct RIGHT-join match tracking.

# Memory (gen1)

## State
- Round 1: engine is the stock baseline (ledger empty). Geomean 298ms. Top: q09 1284, q13 834, q18 747, q19 378.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run on this same codebase/workload. Treat them as strong priors (measured), not as already-landed code.

## Prior-run wins to port, in rough priority order (gain / risk)
1. JoinDependentFilterRule before DistributivityRule (optimizer.cpp:52/69): q19 -53%. DISPATCHED r1.
2. contains() length-aware selectivity in relation_statistics_helper InspectTableFilter: q09 -35%.
3. Perfect HJ for RIGHT joins (3 gates): q13 -20%.
4. Substring prefilter over contiguous string runs (LIKE/contains): q13 -11%. SIMD strstr needs an overlapping tail.
5. Join key-set range filter through compress projections: q18 -13.6%. Semi-join RHS-aware estimate: q18 -8%.
6. BF on first key of a multi-key HJ: q09 -21%. Exact bitmap BF for dense int keys: q09/q16/q21 -10..-15%.
7. Large perfect HA (22-bit) + parallel source: q13 -18.6%. Distinct HT partitioned on group hash: q16 -12%.
8. OR-of-ranges as ExpressionFilter, dense mask eval: q19 -7..-11%.

## Known dead ends (prior run)
- HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ, bitpacking select: all ~0%.

## Codebase facts
- Rule registration order lives in src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp (rewriter.rules push_back).
